The gradient of the function $f(x,y,z)$ is defined as

$$
∇f(x,y,z)=\frac{∂f}{∂x}\,i+\frac{∂f}{∂y}\,j+\frac{∂f}{∂z}\,k.
$$

Since $∇f(x,y,z)=F(x,y,z),$ the function $f(x,y,z)$ must satisfy the following system:

$$
\frac{∂f}{∂x}=y{z}^{2},\,\frac{∂f}{∂y}=x{z}^{2}+z,\,\frac{∂f}{∂z}=2xyz+y-2
$$

First, we integrate $\frac{∂f}{∂x}$ with respect to $x.$ Note that the solution should contain an arbitrary function of $y$ and $z:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & =\int \frac{∂f}{∂x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int y{z}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =xy{z}^{2}+g(y,z)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, differentiating the above expression with respect to $y,$ we obtain

$$
\frac{∂f}{∂y}=x{z}^{2}+\frac{∂g}{∂y}
$$

Taking $\frac{∂f}{∂y}=x{z}^{2}+z$ into account, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}x{z}^{2}+\frac{∂g}{∂y} & =x{z}^{2}+z \\ \frac{∂g}{∂y} & =z\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we integrate $\frac{∂g}{∂y}$ with respect to $y.$ Note that the solution should contain an arbitrary function of $z:$

$$
\begin{aligned}g(y,z) & =\int \frac{∂g}{∂y}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\int z\,\text{d}y \\  & =yz+h(z)\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $g(y,z)=yz+h(z)$ in the expression for $f(x,y,z),$ we get

$$
f(x,y,z)=xy{z}^{2}+yz+h(z).
$$

To determine the function $h(z),$ we differentiate $f(x,y,z)$ with respect to $z.$ This gives

$$
\frac{∂f}{∂z}=2xyz+y+{h}^{′}(z).
$$

Taking $\frac{∂f}{∂z}=2xyz+y-2$ into account, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}2xyz+y-2 & =2xyz+y+{h}^{′}(z) \\ {h}^{′}(z) & =-2 \\ h(z) & =-2z+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C$ is a constant.

Consequently,

$$
f(x,y,z)=xy{z}^{2}+yz-2z+C.
$$
